name: Ilford Delta 3200 Professional
notes: iso is the recommended meter setting EI 3200/36; the sheet also gives an ISO speed of 1000/31 to daylight (measured in ID-11 at 20C), hence balance 'daylight'.

Two families of four curves are plotted (page 5, Characteristic Curves), each for 7, 9, 12 and 16 min at 20C, intermittent agitation. Plot 'curves' = Microphen stock: v = the 9 min curve (the sheet's Microphen time for EI 3200 is 9 min, marked recommended), v-microphen-7, v-microphen-12, v-microphen-16. Plot 'curves-ddx' = ILFOTEC DD-X 1+4 (extra plot name: the README has one 'curves' plot per sheet, so this is a second frame with its own axes): v-ddx-7, v-ddx-9, v-ddx-12, v-ddx-16 (the sheet's DD-X time for EI 3200 is 9.5 min, between the 9 and 12 min curves; the choice of Microphen 9 min as v rather than DD-X is a judgement).

Characteristic curves: x axis is RELATIVE log exposure (no absolute lux-seconds, no Log H Ref), y is density, frame bottom = 0 (gridlines every 0.5, labelled 1.0 and 2.0). Densitometry type is not stated. The curves end at relative log exposure about 4.2-4.25 (density 1.8-2.45), still rising.

All four curves of each family merge into one blob below relative log exposure about 0.6 (base+fog about 0.3) and overlap partly up to about 1.0, so their separate values there are only good to about 0.03-0.05 density; where a curve crosses a horizontal gridline the trace can be off by about 0.02.

Spectral sensitivity: 'Wedge spectrogram to tungsten light (2856K)' drawn as a line curve on a 'Sensitivity' axis with ticks 0.5 and 1.0 only, traced as sensitivity/v with numbers as printed (relative; linear or log not stated); frame bottom about -0.12 on that scale; the curve runs about 354-698 nm and is the same shape as the Delta 400 sheet's.

Page 5 also has contrast-time graphs (contrast index against development time, DD-X and Microphen); not curves of the kinds in the README, not traced. No document code (footer 'Page n of 7, Jun 2025'), no granularity figure.
